notes: Regional heat flow ~90 mW/m²; Bouguer gravity low under the range (thick, light crust).
An N-S fault zone of crushed rock wears into a gully and carries groundwater to springs. Resistivity and gravity low.
An E-W fault zone of crushed rock wears into a gully and carries groundwater to springs. Resistivity and gravity low.

A granite batholith 1.7 km across, its crown already bare: magma that cooled slowly kilometres down. Granite domes and tors once uncovered, ringed by baked hornfels. Gravity low (light granite), magnetic high.

A porphyry stock 350 m across, its top already bare: hard granite inside a ring of baked hornfels, standing up as a knob once uncovered. Magnetic high; the mineral belt's ore came from stocks like this.
4 dikes (N-S, N-S, NW-SE, N-S): hard dark sheets that stand up as walls and dam groundwater. Magnetic highs.
A hydrothermally altered zone 320 m across: soft ochre rock that weathers fast (mineral-belt style). Magnetic low.
A hot spring on the fault: +29°C at the vent, heat flow ~532 mW/m². It melts the snow and keeps the ground unfrozen.
3 soluble beds (limestone, gypsum, chalk): where exposed, streams lose water into the ground and the rock slowly dissolves.
